prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules induce proximity between a target protein and the ubiquitin-proteasome system

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B026 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. After the full round-1 exchange the scientific case looks stronger to me, not just more widely supported, because no one has disputed the mechanism itself. A designed small molecule forms a ternary complex with a chosen target and an E3 ligase, and the target is ubiquitinated and destroyed. This is measurable through cooperativity, binding thermodynamics, structure and degradation kinetics, and many laboratories have reproduced it. It is a new capability, event-driven rather than occupancy-driven action, with the generative potential I look for. On the chair's maturity question I apply one standard to every candidate: is the principle established by independent quantitative evidence and demonstrated to work in patients? Approved cereblon-dependent glue drugs show it works in patients, and the mechanism of the PROTAC arm is independently established. The absence of an approved heterobifunctional drug therefore limits the downstream record but does not make the principle premature. On the attribution question, a citation worded in chemical terms (small molecules that induce proximity to the ubiquitin-proteasome system, with no drug named) rests on two anchors: the PROTAC concept and proof of principle (Crews and Deshaies, with Sakamoto and Kim) and the cereblon mechanism that explains the glue arm (Handa, with Ito). Of the omitted people, Ciulli is the hardest omission to defend, since his VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made rational design possible. I still regard that as a refinement of the concept rather than the discovery, and the committee should say openly that the three-person limit, not a merit judgement, drives the omissions.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection stands: no PROTAC is approved, so a citation that leans on the heterobifunctional arm rests on a trajectory rather than a record, and the clinical history of glues preceded their mechanism. The cereblon work is partly pharmacology, as Somfai notes, and the core chemistry of PROTACs is linker and ligand design on known E3 ligands, which a chemist could call incremental next to a new reaction. The two arms are partly distinct achievements, so the citation can be read as covering a line of work rather than one discovery. Finally, the trio leaves out Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and Ito, and some of them would be called decisive by serious colleagues. I weigh these points as real costs but not as grounds to defer, because deferral risks losing the opportunity to credit living founders.

responses.point: Somfai backs B060 (Buchwald and Hartwig) for clean attribution and a distinct C-N bond construction after the 2010 C-C coupling prize, and says he could support B026 if the maturity argument is stated honestly and the chemistry is clearly present.
responses.response: Your attribution argument is the best on the table and I now list B060 as my first alternative, because the ligand-controlled mechanistic work answers the 2010 overlap objection. On your condition, I state the maturity standard plainly: independent quantitative evidence of the mechanism plus demonstrated benefit in patients, which the glue arm meets and the PROTAC arm meets only on the first part. On whether it is chemistry, I would put it this way: a small molecule is designed to catalyse a protein-protein association that the cell never produced, and the ternary-complex cooperativity that governs degradation is a physical-organic property that can be tuned. That is molecular design, not only biology. If the committee finds that wording too generous, your criticism is a fair reason to word the citation around the chemical principle rather than the drugs.

responses.point: Zou ranked B026 eighth in the opening and keeps it as an alternative, wanting the committee to test whether Ciulli belongs in the trio and returning to B026 once the maturity picture is clearer.
responses.response: The question of whether Ciulli should displace Deshaies or Handa is a fair one and I have tried to answer it with the standard of what was discovered and when. Ciulli's crystallography of VHL and of the ternary complex is decisive for rational design, but it builds on a modality that Crews and Deshaies had already proposed and demonstrated, and removing Handa would drop the discovery that unified the glue arm and explained thalidomide. Removing Deshaies would take away a founder of the concept. I do not see a trio containing Ciulli that does better on both anchors. Since you place B060 first and say you would revisit B026, I would like to know which specific maturity evidence would change your view, so we can tell whether the disagreement is about facts or about standards.

responses.point: Sparr prefers B031 (condensates, Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen), argues that the game-changer criterion is satisfied by condensates, and asks whether the B026 prize credits PROTACs and glues as one discovery or two.
responses.response: On one discovery or two, I treat it as one because both arms act through the same principle, induced proximity to an E3 ligase, and the cereblon result is what lets a single citation cover the PROTAC and the glue without a four- or five-person list. You are right that the two mechanistic stories are different in history, which is why I would word the citation by principle. On condensates, you accept that in vivo evidence is uneven and that Pappu and Mittag supply much of the quantitative content. That is my remaining difficulty: a prize should rest on a result that will not be rewritten, and the sticker-and-spacer theory, which is the part with predictive content, would be left outside a three-person cap. Your own first alternative is B026, so I would ask whether you can support it in the final configuration.

responses.point: Brzezinski now prefers B026 after moving it up from fourth, but names maturity (no approved PROTAC), the omission of Ciulli, and the partial separation of the glue and PROTAC arms as the real weak points, and asks that the reports show the omissions are defensible.
responses.response: I agree that those are the three real weak points and that the omissions must be justified explicitly rather than assumed. I would treat the approved glue drugs as the clinical evidence for the principle and the independent ternary-complex measurements as the evidence for the mechanism, and say openly that the PROTAC arm lacks approval. I also share your reluctance to let enthusiasm for a drug field displace a mechanism-level result such as B028. I read B028 as secure scientifically but with a thinner record of changing what chemists do, which is the reason I rank it below B026. If you think the Gray and Winkler attribution is secure against Dutton and Moser, I would like to hear the argument for the credit boundaries.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat the missing PROTAC approval as a maturity gap that should delay the prize, or accept approved glues plus independent mechanism as sufficient.
Whether the expert reports establish that Ciulli's work is decisive enough to displace Deshaies or Handa, or whether it is a refinement of the concept.
Whether the citation should be anchored on the PROTAC concept or on the induced-proximity principle that includes cereblon, and whether a chemistry-worded citation avoids the pharmacology objection.

Whether B067 or B060 is the better fall-back: B067 turns on whether the reversible-terminator chemistry is separable from 454, Mayer and Ju, and B060 turns on whether it is distinct from the 2010 prize.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to any credited person in B026, B060 or B067 is apparent from my profile, and none of them is at Lund or in the NanoLund network that I know of. My nanophysics background may bias me toward thermodynamic-style arguments, such as ternary-complex cooperativity, and toward nanopore-adjacent work (B021), which I do not prefer. As chair I am recording the positions of the members and I do not treat the count of five as a substitute for the scientific case.
